> I read this as Review - Perform a comprehensive, read-only code review of ClientCore and cross-reference with Shared contracts.

<verdict>FAIL</verdict>
<confidence>HIGH</confidence>
<summary>
ClientCore establishes an end-to-end client decode and rendering pipeline using VideoToolbox, Metal texture caches, and Network.framework, but contains critical resource leaks and decoding flaws. Specifically, `ClientAudioPlayer` leaks all allocated `AudioQueueBuffer`s on every audio frame, `VideoDecoder` destroys and recreates the `VTDecompressionSession` on every single keyframe (every 1 second), and `FrameReceiver` discards valid out-of-order UDP chunks arriving before headers. Additionally, AppKit event monitor disposal occurs on background queues, and `FrameReceiver.stop()` unintentionally restarts background cleanup timers.
</summary>

<findings>
- [CRITICAL] Resource Lifecycle / Memory Leak: AudioQueue buffers are allocated per-packet and never freed
  File: Sources/ClientCore/ClientAudioPlayer.swift:34-65
  Evidence: `play(data:)` calls `AudioQueueAllocateBuffer(q, UInt32(data.count), &buffer)` on every incoming audio packet (50–100/s). In `start()`, `AudioQueueNewOutput` is configured with a dummy completion callback `{ _, _, _ in }` that never calls `AudioQueueFreeBuffer(q, buf)` or recycles buffers into a pool. This produces an unbounded native memory leak during audio playback.
  Suggestion: Pre-allocate a fixed pool of 3–4 `AudioQueueBufferRef`s at `start()` or call `AudioQueueFreeBuffer(q, buf)` inside the `AudioQueueOutputCallback`.

- [MAJOR] Correctness & Performance: VideoToolbox decompression session is torn down and recreated on every keyframe
  File: Sources/ClientCore/VideoDecoder.swift:50-106
  Evidence: On every keyframe, the host prepends VPS (32), SPS (33), and PPS (34) parameter sets. In `processNALUs`, receiving PPS unconditionally invokes `createDecoderIfNeeded()`, which executes `VTDecompressionSessionInvalidate(session!)` and creates a brand new `VTDecompressionSession` without comparing `format` against `formatDescription` via `CMFormatDescriptionEqual`. Recreating the hardware decompression session every 1.0s introduces severe pipeline stalls, memory churn, and in-flight frame drops.
  Suggestion: Before invalidating the existing session, check `if let currentFormat = formatDescription, CMFormatDescriptionEqual(currentFormat, format), session != nil { return }` to keep the active session alive across keyframes unless stream parameters actually change.

- [MAJOR] Protocol Consistency & Network Robustness: Orphan UDP chunks arriving before frame headers are permanently dropped
  File: Sources/ClientCore/FrameReceiver.swift:96-103
  Evidence: In `handleFrameChunk()`, `guard frames[chunk.frameId] != nil` immediately drops chunks if the frame header packet has not arrived yet. Under standard UDP packet reordering or jitter, chunks frequently arrive before or interleaved with the frame header packet. Discarding early chunks prevents the frame from ever reaching `isComplete`, causing the entire frame to be lost.
  Suggestion: Maintain a pending/early chunk buffer (or instantiate an incomplete `FrameAssembly` keyed by `frameId` upon chunk arrival) so chunks arriving prior to `FrameHeaderPayload` are retained for assembly.

- [MAJOR] Concurrency & AppKit Lifecycle: `InputSender.stopCapturing()` invokes AppKit monitor removal from background queues
  File: Sources/ClientCore/InputSender.swift:29-32
  Evidence: `NSEvent.removeMonitor(localMonitor)` is called in `stopCapturing()`. When `ClientCore.stop()` is triggered by `tcpChannel.onDisconnect`, it executes on the `eclipticrd.tcp` / `stateQueue` background queue. `NSEvent` local monitor manipulation requires `@MainActor` / main thread execution.
  Suggestion: Dispatch monitor teardown to `DispatchQueue.main.async` or isolate `InputSender` methods to `@MainActor`.

- [MAJOR] Resource Lifecycle / Timer Leak: `FrameReceiver.stop()` restarts a background cleanup timer
  File: Sources/ClientCore/FrameReceiver.swift:76-85
  Evidence: In `stop()`, `cleanupTimer?.cancel()` cancels the existing timer, but the method immediately calls `self.startCleanupTimer()`. This creates and resumes a new 1.0s repeating `DispatchSourceTimer` on `assemblyQueue` that runs indefinitely after the session has disconnected.
  Suggestion: Remove `self.startCleanupTimer()` from `stop()`; only start the timer when a session begins or in `init`.

- [MINOR] Resource Lifecycle: `MetalRenderer` holds a strong reference to `MTKView`
  File: Sources/ClientCore/MetalRenderer.swift:5
  Evidence: `public var mtkView: MTKView?` is declared strong. Because `ClientCore.shared` retains `renderer`, the MTKView and its window/context hierarchy remain retained across view teardowns.
  Suggestion: Declare `public weak var mtkView: MTKView?`.

- [MINOR] Concurrency: Race condition in `ClientCore.startICE` connecting before TCP handlers are installed
  File: Sources/ClientCore/ClientCore.swift:135-138
  Evidence: `tcpChannel.connectICE(endpoints: endpoints)` starts connection attempts before `setupTCPHandlers(host: nil)` is called. If the TCP connection transitions to `.ready` synchronously or rapidly, `onConnect` will fire before the handler closure is attached.
  Suggestion: Call `setupTCPHandlers(host: nil)` before calling `tcpChannel.connectICE(endpoints: endpoints)`.

- [MINOR] Performance: Redundant memory allocations and copies in `VideoDecoder.decodeNALU`
  File: Sources/ClientCore/VideoDecoder.swift:110-130
  Evidence: For every NALU, `decodeNALU` allocates a new `Data` buffer to prepend the 4-byte length header, allocates a `CMBlockBuffer` via `CMBlockBufferCreateWithMemoryBlock`, and copies the bytes via `CMBlockBufferReplaceDataBytes`. The incoming `Data` buffer already had the length prefix prior to slicing.
  Suggestion: Pass the original subdata slice containing the 4-byte length prefix directly into a contiguous memory block buffer to avoid intermediate allocations.

- [MINOR] Protocol Consistency: `FrameReceiver.trackFrameLoss` regresses `expectedFrameId` on out-of-order headers
  File: Sources/ClientCore/FrameReceiver.swift:115-130
  Evidence: If frame headers arrive out of order (e.g. frame 10 then late frame 9), `expectedFrameId = receivedFrameId + 1` resets `expectedFrameId` backwards from 11 to 10, causing frame 11 to subsequently calculate an artificial frame gap of 1.
  Suggestion: Only advance `expectedFrameId = max(expectedFrameId, receivedFrameId + 1)`.

- [NITPICK] Correctness: Audio packet fast-path skips magic header validation
  File: Sources/ClientCore/ClientCore.swift:51-56
  Evidence: `udpChannel.onReceive` inspects `data[2] == PacketType.audioFrame.rawValue` without validating `data[0...1] == ERDConstants.magic`.
  Suggestion: Validate packet length and magic `UInt16` prefix before checking packet type.

- [NITPICK] Configuration: `VideoDecoder` omits real-time decompression session flags
  File: Sources/ClientCore/VideoDecoder.swift:93-106
  Evidence: `VTDecompressionSessionCreate` does not configure `kVTDecompressionPropertyKey_RealTime` on the session.
  Suggestion: Call `VTSessionSetProperty(session, key: kVTDecompressionPropertyKey_RealTime, value: kCFBooleanTrue)`.
</findings>

<solid_points>
- Clean zero-copy texture bridging in `MetalRenderer` via `CVMetalTextureCacheCreateTextureFromImage` for BGRA pixel buffers.
- Correct NDC math, quad vertex ordering, and alpha-blended mouse cursor overlay rendering in `Shaders.metal` and `MetalRenderer.swift`.
- Thread-safe state synchronization on `ClientCore.serverScreenWidth` / `serverScreenHeight` using dedicated serial queues.
- Robust fallback between precompiled `.metallib` default library and JIT dynamic compilation in `MetalRenderer.setupPipeline`.
</solid_points>

<blocking_issues>
1. `ClientAudioPlayer.swift:34-65`: Continuous memory leak of `AudioQueueBufferRef` on every audio frame without `AudioQueueFreeBuffer` or buffer pooling.
2. `VideoDecoder.swift:50-106`: Unconditional invalidation and recreation of `VTDecompressionSession` on every incoming keyframe parameter set.
3. `FrameReceiver.swift:96-103`: Immediate dropping of early/out-of-order UDP chunks preventing frame reassembly.
4. `InputSender.swift:29-32`: Invoking AppKit `NSEvent.removeMonitor` from background queues during session disconnect.
5. `FrameReceiver.swift:76-85`: `stop()` spawning an immortal background cleanup timer on `assemblyQueue`.
</blocking_issues>
